blk_part_01_part_1_a_cathedral_paid_for_.text: To answer that, we first need to know why it was started. The site was already religious. In the 6th century, after Roman rule ended, Merovingian kings built a church for a bishop there. Centuries later, Cologne's archbishops wanted something much bigger. They built the Gothic cathedral and new city walls together. Their aim was to promote Cologne as a "Holy" city and as the capital of their Electorate, the region they ruled. So the cathedral was about faith, but it was also about power and image.
